module_microarchitecture.name: sram_mbist_demo_controller
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Small synchronous register-mapped controller with explicit child SRAM wrapper integration and latched BIST/IRQ reporting. The implementation should keep the memory path visibly tied to the wrapper instance u_sram and avoid any inferred storage or raw SRAM replacement.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Use a single-clock, active-low-reset control plane. Decode writes to CONTROL, STATUS readback, MEM_ADDR, MEM_WDATA, MEM_CONTROL, BIST_CONTROL, IRQ_STATUS, and IRQ_CLEAR directly from the minimal bus-style inputs. Treat MEM_CONTROL.MEM_WRITE and MEM_CONTROL.MEM_READ as one-cycle transaction initiators using the stored address/data registers. Accept BIST requests from bist_start or BIST_CONTROL.START, and allow BIST_CONTROL.CLEAR_RESULT and IRQ_CLEAR to clear latched status.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Maintain only small holding registers and status latches: control bits, MEM_ADDR, MEM_WDATA, software-visible MEM_RDATA, BIST done/fail/running indicators, last_fail_addr, IRQ_STATUS, and a ready/busy indication. The controller should not model the SRAM contents internally; the SRAM is external macro state exposed through the wrapper.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Drive rd_data with register readback data or MEM_RDATA as selected by rd_en/rd_addr. Drive ready from controller availability, bist_done and bist_fail from latched BIST status, and irq from IRQ_ENABLE gated with latched IRQ_STATUS bits. Ensure reset clears all software-visible outputs and status latches.
ownership_notes: The top module remains a controller and is not a raw SRAM model.
The top-level controller must instantiate demo_sram_32x256_wrapper as child memory wrapper instance u_sram.
Do not infer, substitute, or model the scratchpad as a register array.
BIST status registers remain architecturally present regardless of any future MBIST wrapper insertion.

module_microarchitecture.name: demo_sram_32x256_wrapper
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Simple functional SRAM wrapper that preserves explicit qualified macro binding and exposes a one-functional-access-path interface around the prebuilt Sky130 SRAM macro.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Translate the wrapper inputs clk, csb, web, addr, din, and the reserved/read-port signals into the qualified macro port contract. Keep the second read port safely tied off or reserved. Use the wrapper as the only memory-facing child of the controller.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: No internal memory array or fallback storage is permitted. The wrapper is a structural/synthesis-friendly binding layer only, with memory state residing in the qualified macro collateral.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Forward the macro read data to dout. Leave dout1 unconsumed. Tie wmask0 to 4'b1111 for full-word writes and preserve explicit qualified macro instantiation as u_sram.
ownership_notes: The wrapper must instantiate sky130_sram_1kbyte_1rw1r_32x256_8 as u_sram.
Do not generate or instantiate an inferred array, alternate SRAM, demo_sram_32x256_model, or fallback memory identity.
If the qualified macro behavioral collateral is unavailable, the journey should fail rather than substituting another memory.
The wrapper is a child module and not a replacement for the controller.

sequencing_notes: After reset deassertion, all control and status registers are cleared and ready is deasserted until the controller is available for a new transaction.
A write to MEM_ADDR or MEM_WDATA updates the corresponding holding register without directly accessing the SRAM.
A MEM_CONTROL write with MEM_WRITE asserted performs a functional write using the stored MEM_ADDR and MEM_WDATA through the wrapper access path.
A MEM_CONTROL write with MEM_READ asserted or a readable rd_en/rd_addr access returns memory readback through MEM_RDATA/rd_data without exposing undocumented locations.
BIST can be requested by bist_start or BIST_CONTROL.START; the controller should latch done/fail outcomes and record last_fail_addr when applicable.
BIST_CONTROL.CLEAR_RESULT and IRQ_CLEAR clear latched BIST/IRQ status as specified.
irq asserts only when IRQ_ENABLE is set and at least one IRQ_STATUS bit is latched.
The functional memory access path should remain single-ported from the controller perspective, even though the underlying macro is 1RW1R.
timing_notes: Use clk as the single synchronous control clock for the controller and wrapper integration path.
Treat reset_n as an active-low synchronous or reset-qualified control input consistent with synthesizable implementation intent.
Assume SRAM read data is produced according to the qualified macro timing collateral; the controller should only expose the wrapper output rather than emulate array latency.
Tie-off of the reserved second read-port inputs must be static and safe for synthesis and downstream MBIST collateral generation.
consistency_notes: No hierarchy, ports, or filenames may differ from digital_spec_json.
